claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is driven by nanoscale chemical-order clusters coupled to localized lattice strain.
Chemical-order clusters and localized lattice strain enhance local magnetic exchange interactions.
Chemical-order clusters and localized lattice strain enhance spin fluctuations.
Enhanced exchange interactions and spin fluctuations produce a large entropy change near the magnetic transition.
The proposed ordering-and-strain mechanism preserves rapid thermal exchange.
The proposed ordering-and-strain mechanism preserves low hysteresis.
The proposed ordering-and-strain mechanism preserves mechanical stability.
The initial as-cast or rapidly quenched alloy has a largely homogeneous elemental distribution with incipient short-range chemical order.
Controlled annealing promotes nanoscale chemical ordering.
Controlled annealing relaxes lattice strains.
Ordered domains help maintain rapid heat exchange.
Ordered domains minimize hysteresis losses.
Ordered domains avoid degradation of mechanical stability.
Relative to the as-cast state, annealing should increase magnetic entropy change at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
Relative to the as-cast state, annealing should increase the adiabatic temperature change at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
Relative to the as-cast state, annealing should reduce magnetic hysteresis during the phase transition.
Relative to the as-cast state, annealing should maintain or improve thermal conductivity.
Relative to the as-cast state, annealing should maintain or improve mechanical properties.
The mechanism should apply to sufficiently high-chemical-entropy transition-metal compositions with minimal or no rare-earth content near their magnetic transition temperature.
Extreme compositions or thermal regimes may not exhibit the proposed effects.
